instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment.
Bring a medium pot of water to a boil. Meanwhile, fill a large bowl with cold water.
Add the broccoli to the boiling water and cook it for 1 minute, until it's bright green.
Drain the broccoli and transfer it into the cold water for 1 minute. Drain it well and pat it very dry with a clean towel. Wet broccoli makes soft tots that fall apart.
Chop the broccoli finely, into pieces no bigger than 1/4 inch. Stop before it turns to mush.
Dice a quarter of the onion finely. That should be about 1/4 cup.
Shred the cheddar and chop 2 tbsp of the parsley.

Beat the egg in a large bowl. Add the broccoli, onion, cheddar, parsley, 1/3 cup panko, 1/3 cup Italian breadcrumbs, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Mix until it holds together when you squeeze a little in your hand.

Scoop about 1 1/2 tbsp of the mixture, squeeze it firmly into a ball and shape it into a little log. Set it on the baking sheet. Make the rest the same way. That should be about 20. Rinse your hands every few tots if the mixture sticks.
Bake the tots for 10 minutes. Flip them and bake the other side for 10 to 12 minutes, until they're golden brown and crisp.
Let them sit on the sheet for 2 minutes. Serve hot with the ketchup.
method_notes: All three versions briefly blanch the broccoli, chop it fine, bind it with an egg, cheddar and breadcrumbs, shape small tots and bake them at 400°F, turning them halfway. Gimme Delicious (the lead) uses both panko and Italian breadcrumbs with onion and parsley; Chef Savvy adds parmesan, garlic powder and onion powder, and Skinnytaste adds scallions and an extra egg white. This follows the lead with a little more cheddar, 1/2 cup instead of 1/3, and ketchup on the side as all three serve it.
